question: What is the mascot of Expo 2025 in Osaka?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Myaku-Myaku**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Myaku-Myaku** is the official mascot of Expo 2025, which will be held in Osaka, Kansai, Japan.
 
• The mascot was unveiled on **July 18, 2022**, as part of the promotional efforts for the event.
 
• Its design represents the concept of **"co-creation of a future society for our lives"**, reflecting the theme of Expo 2025.
 
• The character is a vibrant and fluid-like entity symbolizing the **flow of life, connection, and coexistence** among people, nature, and technology.
 
• Myaku-Myaku has gained significant attention for its **unique and abstract design**, which stands out compared to traditional mascots.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Expo 2025 Overview**

 
 
• Expo 2025 will be held in **Osaka, Kansai, Japan**, from April 13 to October 13, 2025.
 
• The theme of the event is **"Designing Future Society for Our Lives"**, emphasizing sustainability and innovation.
 
• It aims to address global challenges by fostering dialogue and collaboration between nations, organizations, and individuals.
 
 
 
• **World Expos**
 
 
• World Expos are large international exhibitions held every five years to showcase achievements in science, technology, culture, and innovation.
 
• The first Expo, known as the Great Exhibition, was held in **London in 1851**.
 
• They are regulated by the **Bureau International des Expositions (BIE)**, headquartered in Paris.
 
 
 
• **Japan and World Expos**
 
 
• Japan has hosted multiple Expos, including **Expo 1970 in Osaka**, which was the first World Expo held in Asia.
 
• The 1970 Expo's theme was **"Progress and Harmony for Mankind"** and attracted millions of visitors.
 
• Expo 2025 is expected to build upon Japan's legacy of innovation and cultural exchange.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Myaku-Myaku**
 
 
• The mascot's name, "Myaku-Myaku," is derived from the Japanese word for **"pulse" or "flow,"** symbolizing continuity and life.
 
• Its design reflects the Expo's emphasis on **sustainability, diversity, and inclusiveness**.
 
• The character serves as a cultural ambassador, engaging audiences worldwide and promoting the Expo's goals.
